query: How do we combine micro cohort CLV counterfactuals with macro panel elasticities to allocate cumulative revenue gains across channels and time in a consistent, auditable way?

response.query: How do we combine micro cohort CLV counterfactuals with macro panel elasticities to allocate cumulative revenue gains across channels and time in a consistent, auditable way?
response.answer: Combine micro cohort CLV counterfactuals with macro panel elasticities using a consistent, auditable model that allocates revenue gains across channels and time by applying elasticity adjustments to cohort-level data.

results.title: Micro MPCs and Macro Counterfactuals
results.content: In this section we use a standard medium-scale New Keynesian model, augmented with durable consumer goods, to show that the leading micro MPC estimates for the 2008 rebate lead to implausible counterfactuals for total consumption and motor vehi-cle expenditures even when we account for general equilibrium forces. In this section, we document and correct for three important upward biases in the Parker, Souleles, Johnson, and McClelland (2013) estimation method: (1) An omitted variable bias from not allowing for lagged rebate effects; (2) a bias from “forbidden comparisons” across cohorts with heterogeneous treatment effects; and (3) a rebate reporting bias stemming from a correlation between lagged expenditure and the report of receipt of a rebate. Thus selection on lagged expenditure in-duces a correlation between a household’s change in expenditure and their probability to report receiving a rebate, which biases the estimated rebate coefficient as we show next. However, in the data we estimate ζX = −575, which suggests that rebates are disproportionally reported for households with unusually low lagged expenditure.

results.title: Micro MPCs and Macro Counterfactuals - Johannes Wieland
results.content: III Macro Counterfactuals from a New Keynesian Model In this section we use a standard medium-scale New Keynesian model, augmented with durable consumer goods, to show that the leading micro MPC estimates for the 2008 rebate lead to implausible counterfactuals for total consumption and motor vehi-cle expenditures even when we account for general equilibrium forces.4 We ﬁrst derive the model-implied counterfactuals and then use forecasts and comparisons with histor-ical drops in consumption to argue that they are implausible. results.title: Bayesian Cohort Retention & Revenue Analysis: Complete Guide to CLV Modeling with PyMC
results.content: Customer AnalyticsComplete Guide to Cohort Revenue & Retention Analysis: Bayesian Modeling Approach. # Complete Guide to Cohort Revenue & Retention Analysis: Bayesian Modeling Approach. * A Bayesian approach brings two major advantages: it forces us to quantify uncertainty (important when working with smaller cohorts) and it gives us flexible tools like binomial likelihoods for retention and gamma models for revenue that align with how the data is generated. * A binomial likelihood to model the number of active users as a function of cohort size and retention. The retention and revenue models coupled by the variable Nactive​ through the latent variables p (retention) and 1/λ (average revenue per user) is what we call the *cohort-revenue-retention model*. Cohort retention analysis, combined with Bayesian CLV modeling, provides a powerful way to move beyond averages and understand the real drivers of customer value. Bayesian Cohort Retention & Revenue Analysis: Complete Guide to CLV Modeling with PyMC.
